_comment: News coverage of data centers and local response to them.
Companion to datacenter_yt, which does the same for YouTube comments.
Both read the same codebook, so their exports carry the same columns and
can be stacked in a spreadsheet.
Neither GDELT nor Google News needs a key, so there is nothing in
repository secrets and no quota to share with anything else.
Phrases with spaces must stay in quotes so the engines treat them as
phrases. subjects are what gets searched; recognize is the wider
vocabulary used to judge whether a result belongs.

topics.label: Data center siting and local response

_relevance_comment: A result is kept when it scores 2 or more: a subject phrase in the
headline is worth 2, each angle word 1 up to 2, a state or county name 1.
Everything else is still stored and can be shown, just marked weak.
_limits_comment: GDELT asks for one request every five seconds and caps any single search
at 250 articles. max_age_days only affects how far back a run reaches;
articles already collected are never dropped because they aged out.
